Package neqsim.process.equipment.reactor

Class AqueousCO2HydrationKinetics

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.reactor.AqueousCO2HydrationKinetics
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class AqueousCO2HydrationKinetics extends Object implements Serializable
Published reversible hydration kinetics for aqueous carbon dioxide in 0.65 molal NaCl.

Soli and Byrne measured the reversible reaction CO2(aq) + H2O <=> H2CO3 from 15 to 32.5 degrees Celsius in 0.65 molal NaCl. Their fitted first-order rate constants are ln(kH / s-1) = 22.66 - 7799 / T and ln(kD / s-1) = 30.15 - 8018 / T, with temperature in Kelvin.

The source did not qualify pressure effects or dense-phase CO2. This class therefore provides the aqueous kinetic bridge and its published temperature/composition boundary, but it does not claim that the correlation is valid at CO2 pipeline pressure. Pressure qualification and phase selection remain caller responsibilities.

Version:
1.0
Author:
NeqSim Team

    • partitionLumpedMolecularCO2

      public static AqueousCO2HydrationKinetics.SpeciationBridgeResult partitionLumpedMolecularCO2(double totalMolecularCO2Concentration, double temperatureK)
      Partition a lumped molecular-CO2 concentration into explicit aqueous CO2 and carbonic acid.

      NeqSim's existing electrolyte reaction sets use a single molecular CO2 inventory for carbonate equilibrium, while this kinetic model distinguishes CO2(aq) from H2CO3. This method provides the source-consistent equilibrium partition needed for reporting or for initializing the explicit kinetic pair. It does not add an H2CO3 component to a thermodynamic system or replace the model-specific CO2water equilibrium constant.

      Parameters:
      totalMolecularCO2Concentration - lumped CO2(aq) + H2CO3 concentration [mol/m3]
      temperatureK - aqueous-phase temperature [K]
      Returns:
      immutable explicit-pair partition
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when the concentration is negative or non-finite, or temperature is outside the published range

    • collapseExplicitPairToLumpedCO2

      public static double collapseExplicitPairToLumpedCO2(double co2Concentration, double carbonicAcidConcentration)
      Collapse an explicit aqueous CO2/carbonic-acid pair to the lumped molecular-CO2 inventory.

      Use this conservation-only handoff before invoking an electrolyte equilibrium model whose reaction set already represents carbonate speciation from one molecular CO2 component. The method does not run hydration, dissociation, charge balance, or phase equilibrium.

      Parameters:
      co2Concentration - aqueous CO2 concentration [mol/m3]
      carbonicAcidConcentration - carbonic-acid concentration [mol/m3]
      Returns:
      lumped CO2(aq) + H2CO3 concentration [mol/m3]
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when either input or their sum is negative or non-finite

    • createReaction

      public static KineticReaction createReaction()
      Create an equivalent generic KineticReaction definition.

      Water is retained in the stoichiometry for elemental conservation but has kinetic order zero because it is the solvent in the published pseudo-first-order model. The returned reaction is not automatically phase- or pressure-qualified. A compatible thermodynamic system must expose distinct CO2, water, and H2CO3 components before evaluating its rate.

      Returns:
      reversible volume-basis reaction matching the published correlations

    • advance

      public static AqueousCO2HydrationKinetics.Result advance(double co2Concentration, double carbonicAcidConcentration, double elapsedTimeSeconds, double temperatureK)
      Advance a closed, isothermal aqueous CO2/H2CO3 pair analytically.

      The exact solution of the two first-order rates is used, so the update is deterministic, non-negative, and conserves the supplied dissolved inorganic carbon without a timestep-size error. It does not perform acid dissociation, charge balance, phase equilibrium, or energy coupling.

      Parameters:
      co2Concentration - initial aqueous CO2 concentration [mol/m3]
      carbonicAcidConcentration - initial H2CO3 concentration [mol/m3]
      elapsedTimeSeconds - elapsed reaction time [s]
      temperatureK - aqueous-phase temperature [K]
      Returns:
      immutable analytical update result

    • relaxationTimeSeconds

      public static double relaxationTimeSeconds(double temperatureK)
      Calculate the analytical relaxation time of the reversible aqueous CO2/H2CO3 pair.

      For the two published first-order rates, any initial deviation from the pair equilibrium decays as exp(-(kH + kD) * t). The corresponding relaxation time is 1 / (kH + kD). This timescale describes only the neutral molecular pair; it is not a bicarbonate, carbonate, pH, phase-transfer, or total dissolved inorganic carbon equilibration time.

      Parameters:
      temperatureK - aqueous-phase temperature [K]
      Returns:
      reversible-pair relaxation time [s]
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when temperature is outside the published range

    • screenResidenceTime

      public static AqueousCO2HydrationKinetics.TimescaleResult screenResidenceTime(double residenceTimeSeconds, double temperatureK)
      Screen the published aqueous CO2/H2CO3 relaxation against a residence time.

      The Damkohler number is the residence time divided by the exact reversible-pair relaxation time. Regime boundaries intentionally match KineticReactionDiagnostics: below 0.1 is transport dominated, above 10 is reaction dominated, and both boundary values are coupled.

      Parameters:
      residenceTimeSeconds - local residence or exposure time [s]
      temperatureK - aqueous-phase temperature [K]
      Returns:
      immutable analytical timescale screen
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when residence time is negative or non-finite, its Damkohler number is non-finite, or temperature is outside the published range
